title: You're a real company when…: Jason Cohen on the milestones that make a startup feel real
summary: Jason Cohen lists the small, tangible milestones that made Smart Bear feel like a real company, from POs and a first employee to a sign on the building. He adds that the pitch even a receptionist can give matters more than polish, and closes with a 2023 story of seeing the WP Engine sign go up.

principles.text: Milestones that make a company feel real are concrete and personal, like a sign on the building, not abstract metrics.
principles.quote: I made one of those bold because that's the one that's always stuck with me. We got the sign about a year ago, and it really was a proud moment.

principles.text: Everyone in the company, even the receptionist, should be able to say what you do and why people buy in about 15 seconds.
principles.quote: The receptionist, by the way, knew exactly what their branch of Adobe (Ottawa) did and could articulate why people bought their products in about 15 seconds.

principles.text: Maturing means accepting enterprise buying norms: take POs, and ship before you get paid.
principles.quote: You take PO's in addition to credit cards, and you've gotten over the fact that, yes, you have to actually ship the product before they give you money.

principles.text: Outsource admin chores like payroll once they're a distraction; it's a sign of growing up.
principles.quote: You pay someone else to print pay stubs and pay your monthly employment taxes because you're just tired of doing it yourself.

principles.text: Growing user counts are a real validation milestone for a small software company.
principles.quote: The 8000'th user of our various software products just came on-line. That makes me feel like a real company.

principles.text: A book can serve as a credibility asset and marketing channel for a software company.
principles.quote: we do have a book with a glossy cover with over 7000 copies in circulation
